newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin still weak, needs time to get well-doctor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin still weak, needs time to get well-doctor.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is still "somewhat weak" after his bout of pneumonia and he needs at least 10 or 15 more days to make a proper recovery, Itar-Tass news agency quoted heart surgeon Renat Akchurin as saying.
But Akchurin, who carried out a multiple bypass operation on the president last November, said the pneumonia posed no risk for Yeltsin's heart.
He said Yeltsin's recovery from the latest illness was going "as it should" and the president was gradually getting better and taking more walks.

Yeltsin, 66, has visited the Kremlin a few times since was taken ill with pneumonia early last month, but he has spent most of his time this year in hospital or in the secluded Gorky-9 residence outside Moscow.
Aides have said many times that he should take things easy.
"Pneumonia is not a joke and there should be no haste in the recovery process," Tass quoted Akchurin as saying.
Tass said that Yeltsin was "somewhat weakened" by the latest illness and he needed time to restore his strength and put on some weight.
Yeltsin, re-elected last July for a four-year term, has looked stiff and aged in television appearances since he started returning to the Kremlin and he has clearly lost a great deal of weight.
His heart problems kept him out of the Kremlin for most of the second half of last year, first while doctors got him ready for surgery in November and then as he recovered from it.
